halfLifeHint: days for a deviation to halve
noiseHint: long-run standard deviation of the spread
real: See it with real data in pairs-trading ↗
pricesAria: Simulated prices of X and Y over {{n}} days; Y tracks β·X.
zAria: Rolling z-score of the spread with entry bands at ±{{entry}} and exit at ±{{exit}}; {{trades}} trades.
pnlAria: Cumulative P&L of the rule: {{pnl}} spread points at the end, {{trades}} trades.
obs: OLS estimated β = {{beta}} (true {{trueBeta}}) and a half-life of {{hl}} (true {{trueHl}} days). Entering when |z| goes above {{entry}} and exiting when it falls below {{exit}}, the rule made {{trades}} trades, {{hit}} of them winners. A short window reacts fast and trades more; if the half-life is long for the window, the z-score stays stretched for a long time.
obsWarn: Note: β uses the whole sample (it looks ahead) and there are no costs and no breakdown of cointegration. In a real pair those are exactly the risks; pairs-trading tests everything out of sample.
note: Synthetic series: X is a random walk and the spread is an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process. No real asset. Educational content, not investment advice.
formulaText: Δt = 1 day. κ comes from the half-life h: κ = 1 − 2<sup>−1/h</sup>. The z-score uses the mean and standard deviation of the last N days of the spread. The rule is short the spread (sell Y, buy β·X) when z is above the entry, long when z is below −entry, and flat once |z| falls back below the exit.
